newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia forms new Japan fishing agreement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia forms new Japan fishing agreement.

text.p: Australian Resources Minister Warwick Parer announced on Monday a new annual fishing agreement with Japan which will allow Japan limited tuna fishing rights in the Australian fishing zone.
"The agreement will benefit both countries and will ensure that all tuna fishing in Australian waters by Japan was conducted under strict management controls," Parer said.
"It will reinforce the important and close relationship between Australia and Japan in the fisheries area."
Under the agreement, Australia would be paid an access fee of A$3.4 million for a maximum of 2,575 days of longline fishing off the eastern coast

The Australian government would give licences to 55 Japanese vessels for the east coast area, the same number as last year, and Japan would retain its voluntary quota of 200 tonnes of southern bluefin tuna in that area.
The number of Japanese vessels licensed to operate off the west coast would be reduced to 15 from 20 last year.
Japanese vessels would be allowed to catch a maximum of 200 tonnes of southern bluefish tuna in the waters around Tasmania, compared to 400 tonnes last year.
They would also be required to release all live blue and black marlin and would continue to be banned from fishing in the area off the north Queensland coast known as area E.
The Australian government has negotiated annual fishing agreements with Japan since 1979.
